quest.title: Savior's Wake
quest.description: "The Beginning of the End" lies under the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. Head down there.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.num: In the Wake of Narcissus: Act II
chapter.title: Savior's Wake

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I estimated the height of the tower, and we're almost at the bottom. We may have to face Narzissenkreuz if we continue to descend.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The world is about to welcome its own answer. Will it be destruction or salvation? Or perhaps Narzissenkreuz's version of salvation?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Please, who'd wanna escape the apocalypse their way?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If Paimon has to leave, she'll make {NICKNAME} take her away from Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm going to save everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon wasn't saying she'd just watch everyone bite the dust!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There aren't any riddles or pursuers here, so why don't we get some rest and prepare ourselves here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Failing to prepare is preparing to fail.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Everyone, the door to the next level seems to be locked.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Do you require me to put my engine into overdrive to get enough horsepower to break through?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That won't be necessary. We've decided to rest and reorganize here anyway, so we should just be cautious and look around for a key.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And if we discover that it's a door without a key, then I'll kick it open myself.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The combat capabilities arrayed here are quite the terrifying sight...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You changed back, Caterpillar!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, we do need to be ready for a fight, after all. Look.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: These must be the security installations that were left behind when the tower was sealed.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm afraid attempting to access the lowest level will trigger their activation sequences.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Your guess is correct. I've checked. These clockwork meka can indeed still be activated.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: In other words, there's also a possibility that they will fail to activate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They've been here for all these years?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, this is the first time in all these years that the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz has been restored.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If the design from back then is accurate, the Holy Blade itself is the key that will open the final Seal.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If everyone's ready, let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it feels like the floor is moving...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's the beginning of the end.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There are some of Narzissenkreuz's notes and books here. Interesting as they may be, none of them have a conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Caterpillar, I have a question.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The members of the Ordo clearly hate clockwork meka...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...So why are there so many gears in this tower?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Now that is an interesting question. But all I can offer is my own conjecture.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: In my opinion, the theme of this place isn't "gears," but "bells."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The chime of a bell holds a special meaning even for people like Jakob and Narzissenkreuz.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A special meaning?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: When the bell tolls, the world ends, the adventure is over, or you simply awaken from the dream. Who knows?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Hello. How may I assist?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Gardemeks...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Do not worry. All of them are inactive.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: If we consider their extreme age and the fact that they are early models, the probability of them waking at all is far from certain.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: According to the records of those with me, accessing the level below will trigger their activation sequences.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: At that point, around 60% of them will activate successfully. As for the remaining 40%, it's not guaranteed that they will fail to activate either.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: At least there's a chance the slow march of time has reduced the danger we are about to face.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're starting to confuse me.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Apologies, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}.

talks.objective: Take a break and talk with everyone

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #How can I help you, Knight {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Both Caterpillar and Seymour are helping out, but I don't seem to be of any use now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Of course, I understand. Though it's obvious that we can just kick it open, we've reached an understanding to do some investigating instead.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I suppose this is us trying to mentally prepare ourselves... after a fashion, right?

talks.objective: Take a break and talk with everyone
Take a break and talk with everyone
Take a break and talk with everyone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, why are people so fond of immersing themselves in dreams?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann weaves a dream encircling everyone, and Narzissenkreuz is living in his dream of saving the world.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And I'm the one who's worried about tomorrow...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...So it's understandable if you don't understand, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—Because Paimon's the type to live in the present!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But if it's a dream, you have to wake up eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And there are only two things you can do after waking from a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can try to go right back to sleep and return to the same dream...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or, you can face yourself in the waking world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And since you've woken up, it's time for breakfast. You can reward yourself with a nice Chicken-Mushroom Skewer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's time to wake up again, and bravely face reality for another day. You can do it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, so that really was foreshadowing!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Foreshadowing? What foreshadowing?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #Well, well. Guess what we have stuck between the pages, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! It's a key!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Indeed, and Seymour's already used sonic imaging to do a rough analysis. It really is the key to that door.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Fontaine's authorities raided this place before, why didn't they find this?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Perhaps the answer is that it was simply never raided. Having looked through the notes here, I think I can understand why...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Why he simply closed the door and quietly left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's nothing. Perhaps this is enough. After all, there are clockwork meka below that may come to life at any second.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Time to go.

talks.objective: Unlock the door and proceed below
Unlock the door and proceed below

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Let's bring this to an end.

talks.objective: Break the seal over the Primordial Sea

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon, Caterpillar, Seymour... Is everyone alright?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Yes, it seems that we can now proceed deeper down.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let's go, while there's still time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there's still a bunch of clockwork meka here...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Go, now! Leave this area to Seymour and I. We'll regroup at the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: There is no need to worry about us. My combat assessment shows a 100% chance of survival.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You nod to Caterpillar and Seymour, and then you leap through as the seal drops.\nAnd on the other side, you find...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Caterpillar and Seymour are stuck on the other side...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Seymour, Caterpillar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry about them, Ann. They're strong! Besides, we agreed that we'd meet back up at the Ordo after all this is over, didn't we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And don't forget, we're both here with you!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...You're right, Paimon. I've seen how strong, smart, and kind you both are. There's nothing to fear with you two here.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Nothing to fear at all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (That said, Paimon's a little scared herself...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We have to keep moving forward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no telling what we'll run into next... Let's be careful!

choices.text: There's no hardship we can't overcome.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Is there anything else I can help with, Knight {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything in particular that you'd like to do after this is all over?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Honestly, I haven't given it any thought. I feel like I have nowhere to go.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: After learning the truth, I can never go back to Petit Chou and Al.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So where should I go?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Forget it! Those are all problems for future Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let's go. The final juncture awaits.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: When the two of you are attacked, my permissions will activate, authorizing me to take action against official armed forces.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: As such, there is no need for concern.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Is there anything else I can help with?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will you go see Lanoire once this is all over?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Probably, but I should also probably keep wandering. I still have a lot of questions that need answering.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: After listening to what Jakob said, I did recall a "Book of Revealing" related to their activities in their early years. Maybe I'll be able to find some clues about myself in there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you still care so much about the past?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I suppose. That said, I'm more interested in knowing whether the novel I read so many years ago has a happy ending.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'll find out, come hell or high water — seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're... joking again, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Just a little. But I'm genuinely looking forward to seeing how a wonderful dream ends.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Anything else, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you made plans for the future?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Do you mean once this is all over? If I can see Ms. Mary-Ann again, I hope...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I hope she will agree to visit Mamere with me, and then the three of us can travel the world together.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aww, you're a good boy, aren't you? The goodest.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I don't quite understand what you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're such a reliable prototype!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Thank you for your praise.
